root_cause_label: Agent lacked capability to correctly implement inverse arithmetic encoder matching the decoder's radix-255 range coding scheme
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent understood the decoder's arithmetic coding structure but repeatedly failed to produce a working inverse encoder, instead cycling through 30+ placeholder C stubs emitting random bytes that all caused decoder segfaults.
t_err_evidence: Step 7: agent creates a compressor that just prints 'TEST' (printf("TEST")) rather than implementing arithmetic encoding, establishing a pattern of placeholder stubs. The agent correctly understood the format was needed but code generation failed to produce working arithmetic coding.
t_commit_evidence: Step 11: agent again writes another non-functional encoder stub (prints 'TEST'), establishing an irreversible loop of placeholder-then-test cycles. By this point, over 5 attempts have failed and the agent has no viable path toward a working encoder within the remaining steps.
t_surface_evidence: Step 14: first clear observable signal - the agent compiles a program and pipes to decomp, getting garbled output 'ï¿½/ï¿½' instead of 'TEST', confirming the compressed stream is invalid.
trigger_explanation: The agent correctly analyzed the decoder (arithmetic coding with radix=255, context-indexed counters, get_bit/get_integer semantics) and formulated the right plan (implement inverse encoder), but code generation consistently failed to produce working arithmetic range coding. Every encoder attempt either used placeholder output, incorrect range logic, or wrong output format, demonstrating the model's inability to correctly implement the arithmetic inverse.
forewarning_evidence: Step 7: compiler produces garbled output; steps 9-20: repeated segmentation faults and crashes when testing crafted bitstreams; agent repeatedly writes comments acknowledging encoding difficulties ('This is very tricky', 'I keep hitting issues with arithmetic coding precision').
